exercise.name: Kneeling Scapular Push-up

reference.title: Kneeling Scapular Push-up (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (shoulder blades only; elbows stay straight)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the chest sinks between the shoulder blades, exhale as you push the floor away and round the upper back slightly.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s each way with a short hold at each end

prescription.frequency: 2-4 times a week (often in a warm-up)
prescription.progression: Scapular push-up on the toes, then the push-up plus (full push-up with the extra push at the top)

cues.text: Knee plank: hands under the shoulders, arms straight, knees behind the hips, body in one line.
Keep the arms straight and let the chest sink: the shoulder blades slide together.
Shoulder blades pinched, elbows still straight, neck long.
Push the floor away: the shoulder blades spread around the ribs and the upper back rises a few centimetres.
Hold the spread for a moment without shrugging, then sink again.

mistakes.fix: It is a shoulder-blade move only: lock the arms long but soft.
Keep the shoulders down away from the ears.

mistakes.mistake: Moving the hips or the low back instead
mistakes.fix: Brace the trunk; only the shoulder blades move.
Sink fully and push fully; the chest travels a few centimetres.

kinematics.norm: Arms stay straight; the motion is scapular protraction and retraction only (Ludewig 2004)
Shoulder blades glide from fully drawn together to fully spread around the rib cage (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Chest 28.1 cm above the floor when sunk
kinematics.peak: 36.9 cm when spread (+8.8 cm); upper back (C7) +11.2 cm
kinematics.norm: The chest sinks and rises a few centimetres between the arms (clinical opinion)
Knees, hips and shoulders in one line throughout (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s sink, 0.5 s hold, 1.2 s push, 0.7 s hold
kinematics.norm: Slow and controlled, about 1 s each way with short holds (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #20771, Kneeling Scapular Push-up (male) (movement reference only)
Ludewig, Hoff, Osowski, Meschke and Rundquist 2004, relative balance of serratus anterior and upper trapezius muscle activity during push-up exercises (Am J Sports Med 32(2):484-493)
Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)

cautions: Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: shorten the range and avoid shrugging (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort: make fists or use push-up handles.
Too hard to hold the knee plank: do it standing against a wall.

muscleNotes.serratus_r: Main target: protracts the shoulder blades around the rib cage; push-up plus variations produce high serratus anterior activity relative to upper trapezius (Ludewig 2004; Ekstrom 2003).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Main target: protracts the shoulder blades around the rib cage; push-up plus variations produce high serratus anterior activity relative to upper trapezius (Ludewig 2004; Ekstrom 2003).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Draw the shoulder blades together as the chest sinks, then control them as they spread.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Draw the shoulder blades together as the chest sinks, then control them as they spread.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Pectoralis minor and major help pull the shoulder blades forward.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Pectoralis minor and major help pull the shoulder blades forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the arm position over the hands.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the arm position over the hands.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the trunk still so only the shoulder blades move.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keeps the hips in line with the knees and shoulders.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keeps the hips in line with the knees and shoulders.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Should stay quiet: no shrugging (Ludewig 2004 looked for a low upper trapezius share).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Should stay quiet: no shrugging (Ludewig 2004 looked for a low upper trapezius share).

guides.label: Upper back sinks and rises; arms stay straight
